description: This Java class handles sequences of key events for a hardware keyboard, including mapping QWERTY keys to custom characters, managing key sequences, and processing special keys like shift and alt. It maintains state for multi-tap input sequences and interacts with input handler to modify input text accordingly.

classes.name: HardKeyboardSequenceHandler
classes.description: Handles hardware keyboard input sequences, including mapping QWERTY keys to custom characters, managing multi-tap sequences, and processing special keys like shift and alt. Maintains sequence state and interacts with input handler to modify input text.

methods.name: addQwertyTranslation
methods.description: Maps a string of target characters to the QWERTY key sequence, adding corresponding sequences for each key, including shift-modified characters.

methods.name: addSequence
methods.description: Adds a key sequence that results in a specific character.

methods.name: addShiftSequence
methods.description: Adds a key sequence with a shift modifier that results in a specific character.

methods.name: addAltSequence
methods.description: Adds a key sequence with an alt modifier that results in a specific character.

methods.name: addNewKey
methods.description: Processes a new key event, resets sequence if timeout has elapsed, and updates sequence state.

methods.name: addSpecialKey
methods.description: Handles special key input (shift, alt) and resets sequence if needed.

methods.name: getCurrentCharacter
methods.description: Returns the character corresponding to the current sequence, deleting previous input if necessary, based on sequence matching.
